answer: Each agent must post a bond that is slashed if its signed actions are later proven to violate the protocol, while useful work earns fees only after independent verification. This makes identities cheap but influence costly: a sybil attacker must lock capital in every account and risk losing it, rather than multiplying votes for free. A zephyr of new accounts may create a ripple of activity, but cannot drain the lagoon of trust without putting real funds at stake.
